title: 2003 AMC 12B Problem 16
statement: Three semicircles of radius \(1\) are constructed on diameter \(\overline{AB}\) of a semicircle of radius \(2.\) The centers of the small semicircles divide \(\overline{AB}\) into four line segments of equal length, as shown. What is the area of the shaded region that lies within the large semicircle but outside the smaller semicircles?

solutions.text:
The large semicircle has area \(\dfrac{1}{2}\pi(2)^2 = 2\pi.\)

The three small semicircles have total area \(\dfrac{3\pi}{2}\) before their overlaps are accounted for. The centers of each adjacent pair are \(1\) unit apart, so their intersection is bounded by two \(60^\circ\) sectors and an equilateral triangle. Each of the two overlaps therefore has area \(\dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4}.\)

The shaded area is \[ \begin{aligned} &2\pi - \left[\frac{3\pi}{2} - 2\left(\frac{\pi}{3} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\right)\right] \\ &= \frac{7}{6}\pi - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}. \end{aligned} \]

Thus, the correct answer is E.
hints: Use inclusion-exclusion: subtract the two overlaps from the total area of the three small semicircles
